summary: Instrumented the provider, matching, metadata, artwork, queue, reconciliation, webhook, and lifecycle boundaries with secret-free log calls under the ADR-020 clause 4 redaction contract and bounded log volume (ADR-020 clause 6). Added a plugin-owned src/ArrTags/Logging boundary: IArrTagsLog<T>/ArrTagsLog<T> resolves the host ILogger<T> for the calling type (category = the calling type's name, so every category is prefixed ArrTags.*), gates every call on the task 10.1 ILogVerbosityGate read from the current configuration snapshot, and applies one shared, provider-neutral, thread-safe LogThrottle. Call sites: ConcurrencyLimitedArrMetadataReader<T> (provider read outcome), RadarrMetadataReader/SonarrMetadataReader (match outcome), MetadataReconciliationProcessor (publish/discard/read failure), ArtworkGenerationCoordinator (generation outcome), LibraryWorkWorker (processed/retry/contained failure), LibraryReconciliationService (bounded result summary), WebhookAuthenticationFilter and WebhookIntakeService (auth rejection/resolution/contained failure), and ArrTagsLifecycleService (start/stop/item removal). Only bounded, already-redacted values are emitted (ArrProviderError code/retryability/message, non-secret connection identity, provider kind, bounded match status/method/ambiguity reason, configuration version, bounded outcome/reason enums, bounded item/record identifiers, counts, exception type names); no API key, webhook secret, SecretLease value, X-Api-Key/X-ArrTags-Webhook-Secret header, raw request/response body, full provider payload/DTO, or mutable PluginConfiguration is logged. The emitted data shape is identical at every level (no Trace-only branch), so raising verbosity cannot expand a redacted value into a secret-bearing one. Log volume is bounded by the code-owned LogThrottle (not user-configurable): at most 5 records per category/event per one-minute window, one bounded suppression summary per window rollover, and a 256-key tracking cap; the bound is recorded as a docs/architecture.md section 12 limit row. ArrTagsServiceRegistrator registers LogThrottle and a closed IArrTagsLog<T> for every instrumented type via a factory that resolves ILogger<T> through the host DI and falls back to NullLogger<T> when the host has not registered logging; it registers no custom ILoggerProvider/sink and does not replace the host ILoggerFactory. LogRedactionTests (65 cases) drives every boundary with sentinel secrets at every verbosity level, asserts no sentinel in captured output with exact per-level emission counts, proves a Trace raise adds no message beyond Debug for every boundary, proves the suppression/tracking/thread-safety bounds, proves the MVC TypeFilter construction path receives the registered log, and proves the registrator's ArrTags.* category prefixes and no-logging fallback. Redaction assertions were proven non-vacuous by temporarily leaking the connection URL and the webhook header value at two call sites, which failed 10 cases.

known_limitations: docs/limitations.md SEC-5 is now stale. Exact behaviour: it still states 'the plugin has no logging call sites, so no plugin log path can leak a secret', which was true before task 10.2 but is no longer true because the instrumented call sites exist. Precondition: task 10.2 deliberately did not rewrite SEC-5 because the assigned task and PLANS.md assign the SEC-5 rewrite to task 10.3. Consequence: until task 10.3 lands, SEC-5 is a stale negative claim and must be rewritten to the ADR-020 redaction contract before Gate 10.

The bounded/redacted contract of ArrProviderError.Message is relied upon but not re-verified. Exact behaviour: the provider boundary and the metadata boundary log ArrProviderError.Message, which ArrProviderError bounds to 512 characters and documents as never containing an API key, request URL, or raw provider payload. Precondition: the provider client implementations (RadarrClient/SonarrClient) are the only producers of that message and were not modified by this task. Consequence: if a future provider-client change put a credential into ArrProviderError.Message, the log call would emit it; the redaction tests exercise the boundary with a fixed, redacted message and cannot detect that upstream construction defect.

The actual host Serilog emission and sink output were not live-verified. Exact behaviour: host ILogger<T> resolution, the ArrTags.* category prefix, verbosity gating, and redaction are proven by unit/integration tests over the DI container and a capturing ILoggerProvider; no live pinned Jellyfin host was started in this environment. Precondition: ARRTAGS_JELLYFIN_HOST_DIR is unset, so the 63 host-guarded facts remain skipped. Consequence: a host-specific emission or sink-format issue (for example the logging.json vs logging.user.json naming caveat noted in docs/research/jellyfin-12-architecture.md section 10.2) would not be caught here; live confirmation belongs to the consolidated pinned-host verification (task 14.3).

Boundaries constructed without a log instance emit nothing. Exact behaviour: each instrumented class takes an optional IArrTagsLog<T>? defaulting to null, so a direct construction that omits it is silent; production DI always supplies the registered closed type, and the MVC TypeFilter construction path is proven by a test to receive it. Precondition: only callers that construct the class outside the registrator. Consequence: a new non-DI construction site would silently lose the boundary's logging until it passes the log; this is a diagnostic gap, not a secret-exposure path.

LogThrottle window-rollover semantics drop one message. Exact behaviour: when a window rolls over and the previous window had suppressed messages, the next call emits one bounded suppression summary instead of its own message. Precondition: a category/event that exceeds the 5-per-minute bound. Consequence: at most one ordinary message per category/event per window is replaced by the summary; this is intentional volume bounding, not data loss of authoritative state.
